Where to stay on Grace Bay Feb 2–7, 2027

  • 2 adults
  • 5 nights
  • Tue Feb 2 → Sun Feb 7, 2027
  • Walk to Grace Bay Beach
  • Cheaper than the Tuscany

Prices and availability checked Oct 15, 2026

We looked at 48 places on or near Grace Bay and researched 40 of them in depth: prices for your exact dates, how easy beach chairs really are in February, how good the pool is for swimming, and what recent guests say. Short version: you can get most of what you love about the Tuscany (right on the beach, easy chairs, a pool Dad can swim in) for about $130 to $370 less a night. But the good-value rooms for Feb 2 to 7 are going fast.

The bottom line

Villa Renaissance is the closest match to the Tuscany for less: a quiet, low-key beachfront condo with easy chairs and a long, straight pool. Call to confirm the $836 garden suite. If you'd rather save more, Royal West Indies is the best value right on the beach (about $1,860 less than the Tuscany for the 5 nights). Le Vele has the best price for a beachfront place with a proper pool, but it's next to a construction site. Whichever you choose, ask for a ground floor or an elevator building, and book soon.

Your favourite

The Tuscany bar: what you get for less

The Tuscany is a 30-suite, all-oceanfront condo resort on the quiet, sheltered far-east end of Grace Bay Beach, rated about 4.9/5 on TripAdvisor. The bar it sets: a huge full-kitchen condo, a heated 70-ft pool, plentiful free beach chairs and umbrellas with no early-morning chair saving, and warm concierge-style service. It is expensive because every unit is a ~1,600-2,000 sq ft oceanfront condo (all units are 3BR, and 1BR/2BR bookings lock off the extra bedrooms). On top of that comes 22% in tax and service charge. Its weak spots are no on-site restaurant or spa, no 24-hour staff, and limited dining within walking distance.

What sets the bar

  • Beachfront on a quiet, calm stretch with plentiful free loungers and umbrellas and no chair-saving games
  • Heated 70-ft rectangular pool that is rarely crowded, good for laps
  • Huge 1,625+ sq ft oceanfront condos with full kitchens, screened balconies, washer/dryer and elevators
  • Warm, personal service from named staff, plus daily housekeeping and grocery pre-stocking
Everything we found about the Tuscany
  • Location: far eastern end of Grace Bay Beach. Ocean Club East (with Cabana Bar & Grill) is next door to the west, the Venetian is next door to the east, and Leeward Beach is a 6-minute walk east. The beach is wide and sheltered from the usual east trade winds, so it is often calm and uncrowded.
  • Units: 30 suites in two 5-floor buildings, all oceanfront with screened balconies, full gourmet kitchens and washer/dryers. Official sizes: 1BR 1,625 sq ft, 2BR 1,816 sq ft, 3BR 2,000 sq ft. Oyster says all units are 3BR, with unused bedrooms locked off. Units are individually owned, so decor varies.
  • Pool: heated courtyard pool, 70 ft long and 5 ft deep, with a jet tub. Oyster calls it a 'sleek lap pool' that guests often have to themselves. Pool hours are 9 am-5 pm, which matters for an early-morning swimmer.
  • Beach service: complimentary loungers, umbrellas ('parasols') and beach towels. Reviewers specifically praise the absence of 'save the chair games' (per review snippets).
  • Service and amenities: award-winning concierge, daily housekeeping with daily towel change, grocery pre-stocking, free bikes, a lit tennis court, a gym, BBQs and gated parking. There is no restaurant or spa on site, and Oyster notes no 24-hour staff. Cabana Bar & Grill next door offers beachside and poolside service.
  • Elevators: yes, two buildings of 5 floors with two elevators (confirmed in the Tuscany deep dive).
  • Age: opened in 2006 (confirmed in the Tuscany deep dive). No property-wide renovation date was found.
  • TripAdvisor: about 4.9/5 from about 783 reviews, ranked #2-#3 among Grace Bay hotels (per TripAdvisor listing snippets, Oct 2026; the rank differs by page). Multiple Travelers' Choice awards.
  • Price for February: the official 1BR winter rate is $1,050/night ($850 is the off-season 'starting at' price). A direct-booking promo of up to 10% off for Jan 5-Feb 9, 2027 (5-night minimum) brings it to about $945, roughly $1,153/night or $5,764 for 5 nights with 22% tax and service.
  • Promo that fits their dates: up to 10% off all room types for Jan 5-Feb 9, 2027, with a 5-night minimum (Feb 2-7 qualifies). At the 1BR floor that is about $765 + 22% = about $933/night all-in, if it applies.
  • Availability: an automated check of the Tuscany's WebRezPro booking engine for Feb 2-7, 2027 showed 'no rooms available', but the page sits behind a human-verification step. Treat availability as (unverified) and call 1-866-359-6466.
  • Policies: 50% deposit, refundable with written notice 30+ days before arrival. $100 per extra person. Check-in 3 pm, check-out 11 am.
  • Review takeaway (paraphrased): the beach is quiet and uncrowded, and there are always chairs and umbrellas without any early-morning towel saving.
  • Review takeaway (paraphrased): staff are warm and proactive, including pre-arrival emails to arrange groceries and excursions. Service is a top reason guests return.
  • Review takeaway (paraphrased): the condos are very large, immaculate and fully equipped, and every suite looks straight at the ocean.
  • Review takeaway (paraphrased): the pool is peaceful and often empty. The property can feel almost deserted, which is good or bad depending on taste.
  • Review takeaway (paraphrased): the main cons are no on-site restaurant or spa and a small or dated gym. Oyster also says rates are pricey for a self-catering property.

Noise check

Construction watch

Grace Bay is in a building boom, and four big projects will still be under construction in February 2027. They're all on the west and west-central part of the beach. The beachfront hotels from Villa Renaissance east to the Tuscany had no construction complaints in our research. Work is usually daytime only, but if quiet matters, avoid the hotels right next to these sites or ask for a building on the far side.

!St. Regis Turks & Caicos

Expected done: Opening late 2027

Residential towers going up between Sibonné and The Sands. Guests next door report daytime noise that reaches the beach.

Near: Sibonné Beach Hotel, The Sands at Grace Bay, The Tides Grace Bay

!The Point (Point Grace expansion)

Expected done: Completion goal late 2027

Oceanfront condos and casitas being added to Point Grace. Neighbors reported daytime noise in 2025 and 2026.

Near: Point Grace Resort & Spa, Le Vele Resort

!Andaz Turks & Caicos (Hyatt)

Expected done: Opens April 1, 2027

A new resort at the Bight Reef. February will be the final push before it opens.

Near: Coral Gardens on Grace Bay, The Seagate Residences

!InterContinental & Kimpton (IHG, the Bight)

Expected done: Due 2027

Sister resorts to the new Hotel Indigo. Its beach area was under construction in April 2026.

Near: Hotel Indigo Turks & Caicos Grace Bay (IHG)

Places with a construction note

  • Le Vele Resort: Point Grace's expansion is being built right next door (completion goal late 2027). Guests reported daytime noise in 2025 and 2026.
  • Point Grace Resort & Spa: The Point expansion is being built on the adjoining site (completion goal late 2027). The hotel warns of daytime noise and has moved its beach setup.
  • Hotel Indigo Turks & Caicos Grace Bay (IHG): IHG's InterContinental and Kimpton resorts are being built steps away (due 2027); its beach area was under construction in April 2026.
  • The Sands at Grace Bay: The St. Regis is being built next door on the west side (opening late 2027). Guests report 7am–7pm noise that reaches the beach; ask for an east-side building.
  • The Seagate Residences: Next to the Andaz construction site (opens April 1, 2027).
  • Sibonné Beach Hotel: The St. Regis is being built right next door (opening late 2027). The hotel posts a construction notice, and guests report early-morning noise.
  • Coral Gardens on Grace Bay: The Andaz resort is being built immediately next door (opens April 1, 2027). February 2026 guests reported 7am–5pm noise, and the $599 units are in the building closest to it.
  • Grace Bay Place: Guests reported construction noise nearby in March and October 2026. Ask whether it's finished.
  • Ellipse Resort Grace Bay: Phase 2 (including the pool) is being built beside the hotel and may still be active in February.
  • The Tides Grace Bay: The St. Regis is going up right next door. Guests report noise and construction debris in the pool.
  • Grace Bay Suites ("The All New Grace Bay Suites"): Construction next door was reported in August 2026; status for February is unknown.

The Tuscany on Grace BayEast end · Beachfront · Condo resort$945–$1,150/night91Their favourite · the benchmark

Availability: The 1-bedroom couldn't be checked online. Call, and ask for the Jan 5–Feb 9 direct-booking discount.

The parents' favourite: 30 huge oceanfront condos on quiet east Grace Bay, free plentiful loungers, heated 70-ft pool, no restaurant.

Best for: Couples who prize a quiet beach with guaranteed chairs, a real lap pool and a huge condo, and don't mind a taxi to dinner.

How it scores

91Fit score 91/100 · the benchmark every other place is compared with

Beach10/10
Beachfront on the wide, calm, sheltered and lightly used east end of Grace Bay proper.
Beach chairs9/10
Free, plentiful, no chair-saving, including an April (high-season) report. Attendant setup is not documented, and Jan-Mar evidence is thin.
Pool9/10
Heated, 70-ft rectangular pool that is rarely crowded, which is ideal for laps. Docked one point for the 9am-5pm hours.
Cleanliness10/10
Booking.com cleanliness 9.6, and reviewers consistently call units and grounds immaculate.
Newness & condition7/10
A 2006 build that is very well kept, with owner-updated interiors that vary by unit. There has been no property-wide renovation, and there are occasional AC/appliance nitpicks.
Service9/10
Outstanding, personal service with named staff praised often. Booking.com staff score is 9.4, and there is no 24-hour desk.

At a glance

Location
Beachfront on the wide, quiet, sheltered far-east end of Grace Bay Beach (about 265 ft of frontage), with Ocean Club East next door to the west and the Venetian to the east. Central Grace Bay (Regent Village/Saltmills/Graceway) is roughly 1.2-1.5 miles away: guests say about 25 minutes on foot, 5 minutes by car or about 10 by the free bikes. Cabana Bar & Grill is next door.
Walk to dining
25 min to the central Grace Bay restaurants
Type
Condo resort, 30 units
Opened
2006
Condition
Opened November 2006 (TCHTA listing; Grace Bay Realty lists 2006, builder TDMG). No property-wide renovation found; VisitTCI says 'built/refurbished 2010'. Units are individually owned, so decor varies. 2025-26 reviewers call the condos beautifully furnished, 'mint condition' and 'modern and comfortable'. Minor nitpicks: an AC problem on arrival (Apr 2024), minor appliance issues (Dec 2023), a small gym and spotty Wi-Fi when several people stream.

Insider tips

  • Book direct by phone (1-866-359-6466) or email (info@thetuscanyresort.com) and ask for the Jan 5-Feb 9, 2027 promo. Confirm the exact % off and 1BR availability, because the online booking engine sits behind a human-verification check.
  • Units are 3BR condos that can be booked as 1BR or 2BR with the extra bedrooms locked off (Oyster). If the 1BR shows as sold out, ask about a lock-off.
  • The deposit is refundable until 30 days before arrival (about Jan 3, 2027). Consider travel insurance.
  • Send a grocery list at least 4 days before arrival for pre-stocking.
  • The pool opens at 9am. The February sea is about 78F, so the heated pool is the better lap option.
  • Use the free bikes, or Grace Bay Car Rentals (10% discount for Tuscany guests), to get to dinner in town.

Large freeform (bell-shaped) heated saltwater family pool fronting the beach, with mosaic tiling, loungers and cabanas. It contains a straight rectangular section of ~22 m x 4 m (~72 ft), 4-6 ft deep, heated to about 82F, usable for laps but unstriped. There is also an adults-only saltwater pool (~19 m x 6.5 m, ~62 ft rectangle) by the West Deck and a family paddle pool.

Three heated freshwater pools. The all-ages Villas Pool is roughly rectangular, about 75-80 ft long and 25 ft wide (OSM outline), with a built-in whirlpool and swim-up bar; it is the best bet for lengths, early in the day. The adults-only (16+) Hotel Pool is an infinity-edge pool with a separate whirlpool; its outline is irregular (~70 ft overall with a narrow ~50-ft arm). The Estate Pool is for Estate guests only. No dedicated lap pool, and no reviews mention swimming laps.

At a glance

Location
On Lower Bight Rd at the quiet western tip of Grace Bay (technically the Bight Beach, a few hundred metres west of the Bight Reef). Bight Reef/Coral Gardens snorkelling is about a 7-minute beach walk (official). Wymara Villas and the Sunset Cove beach club are a separate site at Turtle Tail, a 2.5-mile drive away.

Main-resort guests get one large pool: a 7,000 sq ft mosaic-tiled infinity-edge pool at the heart of the resort, plus a hot tub. It has gradual sitting ledges, four rentable floating island pods and palm planters in the water, so it is a resort pool rather than a lane pool; a Feb 2024 visitor still found it big enough for laps. The 25-metre (82 ft) lap pool is confirmed villa-only: it sits in the Sunset Cove Beach Club at Wymara Villas (Turtle Tail), 2.5 miles away, which the official site says is reserved for registered villa guests. Next to it is a 130 x 30 ft tidal saltwater ocean pool. Resort guests used the ocean pool in 2023-24, and autumn 2026 offered a $50 per person Sunset Cove day pass, but February 2027 access is unconfirmed.

  • Studio Ocean View showed only 1 left for Feb 2-7 on Oct 15, 2026, so book soon.
  • Head to the beach before 10am in peak season to get towels and your pick of shade.

Pros and cons for you

Pros
  • Beachfront on a wide, prime central stretch of Grace Bay, with free loungers and umbrellas
  • Walkable to Ports of Call, Graceway Gourmet and central Grace Bay restaurants
  • Spacious condo suites with kitchens, screened balconies and daily housekeeping
  • Friendly staff with named praise in 2026 reviews, and a loyal repeat clientele (Oyster)
Cons
  • For Feb 2-7, 2027 the official engine had only one 2-bedroom suite left at $1,065/night + 27%; studios ($645) and junior suites ($760) were sold out online
  • Lagoon-style pool with bridges and an island isn't lap-friendly, and heating is unconfirmed
  • No elevators; ground-floor suites are limited and not guaranteed
  • 1999 build with no resort-wide renovation; 2026 reviews mention tired units, low water pressure and worn beach furniture
  • 27% tax and service is added, more than the 22% at the Tuscany

Pros and cons for you

Pros
  • True beachfront on central Grace Bay, with dinner and shops 6-10 min on foot
  • Live Feb 2-7 quote of $618/night (about $785 all-in), well below the Tuscany's ~$945 February rate
  • Chairs, towels, palapas, beach attendants, bikes and water sports all included
  • Rooms and bathrooms freshly renovated 2023-25; heated main pool renovated 2022

Cons
  • St. Regis construction directly next door (opening targeted for late 2027), so a Feb 2027 stay will very likely overlap active work; reviews report 7am-7pm noise audible on the beach
  • No lap pool: main pool is rounded free-form and family-busy; length unpublished
  • 27% in taxes and fees (12% tax + 10% service + 5% facility fee), versus 22% at Tuscany
  • Cheapest Courtyard junior suite has a queen bed, courtyard view and no washer/dryer
  • Shade is limited: about 20 first-come palapas for 114 suites; family-heavy resort
  • Only one of six 3-story buildings has an elevator

Insider tips

  • Ask for a unit in a building on the east side, away from the St. Regis site to the west. Get the expected Feb 2027 construction hours in writing before the 21-day cancellation deadline.
  • Request the elevator building or a ground-floor unit; only one building has an elevator.
  • For $132/night more, the Junior Suite Gardenview adds a screened balcony and in-suite washer/dryer over the Courtyard junior suite.
  • Palapas are first come, first served, so head down early if you want shade in front of the resort.
  • Book Hemingway's dinners ahead (the resort recommends it); there is live music on Tuesdays.

At a glance

Location
On Lower Bight Rd, next door to Wymara, about 1,500 ft west of the Bight Reef snorkel site (VisitTCI). The beach is wide, calm and quiet, but this is the Bight end, not central Grace Bay; VisitTCI notes seagrass starting a short way offshore on the Bight. A boardwalk crosses a lawn and dune from the buildings to the sand (official map). Regent Village is about 3.3 km away in a straight line, so roughly a 45-50 minute walk (my estimate); Oyster calls it about a 10-minute drive.

Cleanliness
2026 Google and TripAdvisor reviewers call the rooms and pool clean, and Google tags 56 reviews on cleanliness. We found no recurring dirt complaints in the reviews we could read, but the sample was small.

Staff friendliness is the most frequent praise, along with easy check-in and daily housekeeping. One Aug 2026 reviewer rated service pleasant but below resort level.

Steady: TripAdvisor 4.4/5 (1,613 reviews) and Google 4.5/5 (532). Mid-2026 reviews are mostly 5s, with a few 3s about heat, the distance to town and the lack of a spa.

Pros and cons for you

Pros
  • Same calm east-end beach as the Tuscany (next door) at about $787/night all-in for the studio, roughly $250 less than the Tuscany 1BR

Insider tips

At a glance

Location
1 Stubbs Rd, at the far-west end of Grace Bay proper, right beside the Bight Reef (Coral Gardens) and the public Stubb's Road beach access. 435 ft of frontage, but the beach is narrow. The water is calm and sheltered, with a sandy entry. Official aerial photos show darker reef and seagrass patches a short swim out, and the reef's roped conservation zone sits alongside. So it suits wading, floating and snorkeling better than long sandy-bottom swims. VisitTCI warns of tubing and wake boats speeding just outside the swim zone, and snorkelers from the public access crowd this stretch. Regent Village/Saltmills is about 2.7 km away in a straight line (my estimate from coordinates): roughly a 35-40 minute walk or a 5-10 minute taxi.

Cancellation
Standard period (Jan 3-Dec 18, 2027): a 3-night deposit is due at booking. It's refundable, less a 5% card fee, with written cancellation 30+ days before arrival, and forfeited after that. No-shows pay 100% and early departures are charged in full. The Advance Purchase rate needs 100% prepayment.
Deals
Members rate (free sign-up): 5% off the lowest published rate. For Studios it equals the Featured rate; for suites it undercuts the 35%-off Early Booking Bonus for Jan 4-Feb 11, 2027 stays, which was still selectable on Oct 15, 2026. Repeat guests get 10% by phone. There is no resort fee.

Insider tips

  • Create the free Members login before booking: on suites it undercuts the 35% Early Booking Bonus (Jan 4-Feb 11, 2027 stays).
  • Book the Studio on the refundable Featured or Members rate, which includes breakfast and is cancellable 30+ days out, not the prepaid Advance Purchase rate, which is priced at rack.
  • Studios are in older buildings 1-2. The 1BR Bungalow ($716-752 Members rate, 725 sq ft, full kitchen) offers more space, but it's a second-floor walk-up with no elevator, about 2 minutes from the beach.

Insider tips

  • Book direct: the cheapest 2BR (Ocean View) wasn't offered on Booking.com for these dates, and the resort offers a price match.
  • Ask for a 'Deluxe' (2024-renovated) unit if condition matters.
  • Recheck availability: a Garden Studio would be $1,030/night all-in for these dates, and shifting to Feb 3-8 currently opens a 1BR Garden Suite at $1,119.
  • Reviewers say à la carte dinner slots fill quickly; book them as soon as the system opens.
  • Owner rentals in the buildings (Airbnb/VRBO) are room-only, but the resort says they get only the apartment, pool, parking and the public beach, not the all-inclusive amenities.

At a glance

Location
Inland at 11 Sandcastle Rd in Grace Bay Village, next to Graceway Gourmet supermarket. The guest beach section sits by The Deck and Solana! on central Grace Bay: the old official site says a 3-minute/300-yard walk, Booking.com says 1,250 ft. A free 8-seat golf-cart shuttle runs (hourly per a 2026 profile). Regent Village is about 0.5 km west (~7 min walk); the hotel's own plaza has Skull Rock, Tribe and Giggles.

Hotel, 103 units
Renovated
2025 · $1M two-year refresh finished early 2025 (new furniture in most rooms, lobby, poolside bar, gym, breakfast room), after a $2M 2023 project (70 rooms redesigned, pool heating added) and 2020 tiling/doors. Painting and interior work was under way in mid-2026. On joining Hilton's Tapestry Collection (Sept 2026) it announced another renovation of the lobby, fitness centre and shared areas 'over the next year', with the hotel staying open.

Older two-building, three-storey walk-up layout (operated as a Comfort Suites before 2011) that has been steadily refreshed; about 80% of rooms have new furniture. A Feb 2025 reviewer called it 'looking tired' and two early-2025 reviewers reported musty odours; 2026 reviewers describe rooms as clean and updated. Studios are 295-325 sq ft with mini-fridge and coffee maker; there are no elevators (a bellman carries luggage).

Praised for
  • Front-desk manager Brenda is named in most positive reviews; Susie (reservations) and Solomon are also singled out.
  • Large suites with full kitchens, dishwashers and in-unit washer/dryers; daily housekeeping.

  • Strong value compared with big Grace Bay resorts.
Complaints
  • Construction next door (St. Regis): noise, smell and daily debris in the pool and on balconies (2026).
  • Elevator reliability: a couple trapped about 40 minutes on Jan 31, 2026 with a non-working emergency button; another guest advised checking whether the elevators work.

Polarised. TripAdvisor's cleanliness sub-score is only 3.3/5, driven by 2024 complaints (dirty floors, stains, bugs). Most 2025-26 reviews call the suites spotless or very clean, but mid-2026 reviews still mention bugs and a poorly kept pool.
Service
Front-line staff get warm, named praise (Brenda above all) and are consistently called friendly and helpful. Management's handling of problems is the weak spot: no medical help after the elevator incident, a refused AC discount and confrontational refund disputes. 2025-26 reviews are mostly 5/5 (Expedia-fed reviews from Mar-Apr 2026 are nearly all 10/10), up from a rough late 2024. But every 2026 low score is about construction, the elevator, the AC or the pool, and the construction will still be under way in Feb 2027.

Pros and cons for you

Pros
  • About $405/night pre-tax (about $2,470 for 5 nights all-in) for a 725 sq ft 1-bedroom with full kitchen and washer/dryer: less than half the Tuscany's rate.
  • Free beach chairs and umbrellas set up daily on a quiet stretch of Grace Bay about 3 minutes' walk away, plus a free golf-cart beach ride for seniors.
  • Newest-build value option (opened Dec 2021) with warm, personal front-desk service.
  • Bay Bistro is next door; Hemingway's at The Sands and the Thursday Fish Fry are walkable.
Cons
  • St. Regis 12-storey towers are under construction right next door (phase 1 not due until late 2027), so expect noise, smells and debris in the pool during a Feb 2027 stay.
  • Elevator safety and reliability: a couple was trapped about 40 minutes in Jan 2026 with a dead emergency button. Older guests should insist on a ground-floor unit.
  • Not beachfront, with no beach attendant and a small chair supply; peak-season shortages have been reported.
  • The pool is modest, with planter islands, unknown length and recent upkeep complaints; not a dedicated lap pool.
  • About a 15-minute walk to the Grace Bay dining strip, and the OTA rate is effectively non-refundable.

Insider tips

  • Request a ground-floor 1 Bedroom Pool View suite so you never need the elevator. These open straight onto the pool deck, so expect to keep the curtains drawn for privacy.
  • Ask the front desk for the complimentary golf-cart ride to the beach, which is offered to seniors.
  • In early February, head to the beach set-up early. There's no attendant, so if every chair is taken, go back to the front desk rather than waiting on the sand.
  • Before booking, ask about the St. Regis construction hours and which units face the site.
  • Avoid the separate 3-bedroom 'villa' (an older house); several reviews describe it as run-down.
  • Repeat-guest and other discounted rates are booked by phone (+1 888 200 7590); if possible, get a refundable rate rather than the non-refundable OTA price.

Huge family all-inclusive on the calm west end of Grace Bay; 10 pools but no real lap pool, and Grace Bay's best-documented 6-7 am chair-saving war.

Best for: Multigenerational families with kids who want everything on site; a weak fit for a retired couple seeking easy chairs and lap swimming.

Beach8/10−2 vs Tuscany
Beachfront on the sheltered west end of Grace Bay with clear water and Bight Reef snorkeling nearby. Marked down for crowds, guest reports of rocks or seagrass along parts of the frontage, and one guest's report of stair-only beach access.

Free loungers but no attendant setup. Most Jan-Mar 2025-26 seating reports describe towels down by 6-7 am, a weakly enforced no-saving rule, butler pre-claiming, scarce shade and paid cabanas.

Ten pools, some heated, but none built for laps. The French Village pool is the closest thing to a swimmable rectangle; the rest are lagoon, play or party pools, crowded with kids in peak season.

At a glance

Location
Beachfront at the western end of Grace Bay (Lower Bight Rd), near where the Bight Beach and Bight Reef snorkel site begin. Sprawling site (about 75 acres): the cheapest French Village rooms sit back from the sand, a few minutes' walk, and an Oct 2026 guest says beach access is by stairs with no ramps. Regent Village is about 1.9 km east in a straight line; VisitTCI says the Regent Village/Saltmills dining area is too far to walk comfortably.

A patchwork of ages. Treasure Beach Village is brand new. Feb-Mar 2026 guests call French Village rooms updated, but its bathrooms dated. Caribbean Village rooms are repeatedly described as very dated and worn, some with musty smells. A Mar 2026 guest saw missing tiles in the Caribbean pools and wear on the Italian pool, and a Jan 2026 guest noted rusty waterslide stairs.

Beach chairs

Included free
Yes
Fee
Loungers are free. Private beach and pool cabanas cost extra (a Mar 2026 guest cites about $200/day) or come with butler-level rooms.
Set up by staff
No
Umbrellas
Some umbrellas and shade at the beach and pools, but shade is scarce; peak-season guests report struggling to find a lounger with an umbrella.
How many
No official chairs-per-room figure. The resort has roughly 850+ rooms (758 before the 101-suite expansion), and one guest says it cooks for 3,000+ at capacity. Demand is spread across a long beach and 10 pools.
Chair saving
Officially no saving: signs at the pools ask guests not to reserve chairs, and a Feb 2025 guest says Beaches promised to clear held chairs. Guests across Jan-Mar 2025-26 say staff rarely enforce it, and butlers reserve chairs and cabanas for their own guests early.

In peak season: Confirmed. In 163 TripAdvisor reviews of Jan-Mar 2025 and 2026 stays, about 32 discuss seating. About 20 of those describe towels on loungers by 6-7 am, with pool chairs (especially the Italian pool) gone by 7-8:30 am. The worst reports come from holiday weeks: UK half-term in Feb 2025 saw chairs reserved by 6 am, once 5:15 am, and a full-capacity Feb 2026 week saw daily arguments over chairs. The beach is easier than the pools. About 12 guests, mostly early risers or quieter weeks (including Jan 29-Feb 5, 2026), had no trouble, and a late-Mar 2026 repeat guest saw better enforcement.

10 pools plus 4 whirlpools and a scuba pool, none designated for laps. The Italian Village pool is the largest (about 15,885 sq ft, zero-entry, swim-up bar), but it is the activity and party pool and is crowded with kids. Treasure Beach Village has a new infinity-edge lagoon pool with sunken seating pods. The French Village pool, a big rectangular pool with shallow kids' ledges, is the best bet for real swimming, ideally early morning before families arrive. Some pools are heated, but guests disagree on how warm.

Praised for
  • Stunning beach and clear water

Cleanliness
Rooms and grounds are mostly praised, with twice-daily housekeeping. There are recurring complaints of cloudy pool water and debris, and of musty or mold smells and stained bathrooms, concentrated in the older Caribbean Village.
Service
Many shout-outs to named butlers, bartenders and housekeepers, but frequent complaints about slow bar service, stretched or curt staff at full capacity, and long dinner waits. Butler-level guests report the smoothest stays.
Recent trend
The TripAdvisor score has held at about 4.3. Treasure Beach Village (Mar 2026) is praised as new and calmer. 2026 reviews still flag dated Caribbean rooms and chair saving, with one late-Mar 2026 repeat guest seeing slightly better enforcement.

Good to know

Know before you go

Background that applies wherever you stay. Tap a topic to open it.

Getting a beach chair on Grace Bay

Grace Bay Beach is public: all TCI beaches are public, with free accesses and parking. However, almost every resort reserves its loungers and umbrellas for its own guests. Whether chairs are hard to get depends on the resort's chairs per occupied room and whether staff enforce a no-saving rule. It is worst at large, busy properties (Beaches Turks & Caicos is the most documented) and easiest at low-density condo resorts on quiet stretches, like the Tuscany, or at luxury resorts where attendants set up chairs for you. Reviews praising easy chairs in summer don't predict February, so weigh reviews from January-March.

  • Legal: 'Currently, all beaches in the Turks and Caicos Islands are public' (TC Weekly News, 2026). The government is drafting CLASP legislation to formalise beach-access rights.
  • Guests only: VisitTCI says 'Most resorts on Grace Bay Beach reserve their loungers for guests staying at the property.' TripAdvisor forum posters report 'resort guests only' signs and staff enforcement (per forum snippets).
  • Walk-up rentals as a fallback: vendors rent loungers and umbrellas at the Central access (near Seven Stars), at the Bight Reef, and at Stubb's Point on Leeward. Delivery services such as Tropical Shades and SandySpot set up on the public sand. This matters for inland hotels or a resort that runs short.
  • Early towel saving: a Providenciales forum thread ('Reserving beach (or pool) chairs?') discusses a 6 am towel-saving routine at some resorts (per forum snippets).
  • Done badly, Beaches Turks & Caicos: the most-documented chair war. TripAdvisor review titles include 'Great resort, need to fix pool chairs/towels' and 'Aggressive guests, Beaches puts people in awkward position', plus a forum thread 'Beach chairs at Beaches Turks and Caicos'. Guests report chairs claimed by 6-7 am and weak enforcement (per review snippets).
  • Done well, attendant setup at luxury resorts: Seven Stars has 'dedicated beach attendants and full service' (official FAQ). Its forum thread 'Beach chairs Seven Stars' reports enough chairs and staff removing unattended items after about an hour (per snippets; unverified detail). Grace Bay Club has 1,100 ft of frontage with loungers, umbrellas and daybeds (Oyster) plus personal concierge service. Point Grace and The Palms are praised for attendants setting up chairs (per review snippets). All of these are usually above the couple's budget.
  • Done well, low-density condos: the Tuscany is praised for no 'save the chair games'. Villa Renaissance advertises 'ample chaises and umbrellas, with no need to reserve in the early morning'. That resorts advertise this shows chair anxiety is a known pain point on Grace Bay.
  • Mid-tier examples: Royal West Indies advertises 'complimentary loungers and umbrellas reserved just for you' (guest-only, with palapa shades). Reviews generally report finding two loungers with shade (per review snippets, through 2024).
  • Seasonality caveat: Ocean Club West reviews about easy chairs are from July-August 2026, which is low season (per review snippets). Don't extrapolate to early February, which is high season.
  • Questions to ask any alternative before booking: How many beach loungers and umbrellas per unit at full occupancy? Do attendants set up chairs, and from what time? Is there a no-saving rule, and is it enforced? Are the shades fixed palapas or moveable umbrellas? Can cabanas be reserved, and at what cost?

Which part of the beach?

Grace Bay Beach proper runs a little over 3 miles. Its western boundary is the Bight Reef (Coral Gardens), with the Bight Beach continuing west, and its eastern end is past the Venetian, where it becomes Leeward Beach. The sand and water are excellent along the whole stretch, and sargassum is rare everywhere because east and southeast winds push it offshore. The segments differ mainly in snorkeling, crowds and walkability. For a couple who wants a great sandy swimming beach and dinner on foot, central Grace Bay is the best fit. Pair it with a resort that has strong chair supply or attendants, since central is the busiest stretch.

  • WEST END / LOWER BIGHT: Coral Gardens and Windsong sit at the Bight Reef accesses. Beaches is about 0.5 mi east of the reef, and the Somerset and Alexandra are on the western side. Wymara and West Bay Club are about 1,500 ft west of the reef, on the Bight Beach rather than Grace Bay proper. VisitTCI warns that many Bight properties market themselves as Grace Bay.
  • West end, water and snorkeling: calm and sheltered. The Bight Reef is the only reef you can swim to from shore on Grace Bay and the most popular snorkel site in TCI: a single coral ridge running about 350 ft out, 15-20 ft deep at its outer end, often with turtles and rays. It has declined somewhat over 20 years, and speeding tubing and wake boats just outside the swim zone are the main hazard. The Bight Beach has seagrass starting about 75 ft offshore, so it is not a pure sand bottom, and seagrass bits occasionally wash up as a thin line.
  • West end, walkability and crowds: a couple of casual cafes at the reef (JoJo's, Somewhere Cafe) plus resort restaurants. VisitTCI says the Bight Beach is 'a bit far for walking' to Grace Bay's shops and restaurants. The reef draws snorkelers and walk-up chair vendors.
  • CENTRAL GRACE BAY: home to the largest resorts and public accesses, including the Central access near Seven Stars and the Grande Court access near Royal West Indies. Also here are the Ritz-Carlton, Grace Bay Club and the Sands (near the Forbes Point access). The walkable 'strip' runs roughly from Le Vele Plaza to One Season Plaza.
  • Central, water: classic Grace Bay with white sand, turquoise water and virtually no rocks or seaweed, protected by a barrier reef about 1 mile out. The reefs here can only be reached by boat. Parasailing and tubing boats operate offshore.
  • Central, walkability: the best on the island. Graceway Gourmet supermarket, Regent Village, Saltmills and Grace Bay Plaza are within walking distance, along with many restaurants (Seven, Coco Bistro, Caicos Cafe, beachfront spots like The Deck, Coralli and Infiniti), two pharmacies and Grace Bay Medical Center, a walk-in clinic with emergency services. Sidewalks are mostly concrete. VisitTCI notes that walks of 15+ minutes are unpleasant in the heat.
  • Central, crowds: the busiest stretch of beach, with the most resort guests, the largest public accesses and rental vendors. Chair supply at your specific resort matters most here.
  • EAST END (Ocean Club East, Tuscany, Venetian, toward Leeward): wide beach, sheltered from the usual east trade winds and often the calmest water. It is quiet and lightly trafficked (VisitTCI, Oyster). Leeward Beach next door is even emptier, but access is limited, rock jetties break it up, and the snorkeling is poor.
  • East end, walkability: limited. Cabana Bar & Grill and Opus are at Ocean Club East. Rickie's Flamingo Cafe is the only non-resort beachfront restaurant on Grace Bay, with public restrooms at its access, and 19 Bar is at the golf club across the road. There is only a small convenience store nearby; the supermarket is about a 5-minute drive, and Grace Bay Village is about a 10-minute bike ride (Tuscany FAQ).
  • Sargassum by segment: Grace Bay, Leeward and the Bight are 'very rarely affected'. VisitTCI's October 2026 update says these lee-side beaches remain largely free even while windward beaches such as Long Bay have heavy accumulation.
  • Fit for this couple: central Grace Bay gives the best swimmable sandy beach plus walkable dining, groceries and medical care. The east end best replicates the Tuscany's calm, chair ease and quiet, at the cost of taxis or a car for most dinners. The west end and Bight are best only if snorkeling from shore is a priority.

Sources: visittci.comvisittci.comvisittci.comvisittci.comvisittci.comvisittci.comvisittci.comthetuscanyresort.comoyster.com

What early February is like

February is the heart of the dry high season: about 81°F highs, little rain, about 7.5 hours of sun a day and a UV index that often hits 12. The ocean is at its coolest of the year, about 77.5-79°F, and trade winds run a bit stronger and choppier than in other months, which makes a heated pool valuable. Sargassum risk on Grace Bay is very low in February. Crowds are lower than December-January but still high season, so book soon and expect minimum stays.

  • Air temperature: average high about 81°F (27°C) and daily average about 77°F (beach-weather.com). VisitTCI calls January-April the dry season, with milder daytime temperatures.
  • Rain: about 2.1 in for the month over about 7.5 rainy days (beach-weather.com), mostly brief showers under 10 minutes. VisitTCI says forecasts more than 2-5 days out are unreliable.
  • Sea temperature: February is the coolest month. The 10-year average is 25.9°C (78.7°F), with a range of 25.3-26.7°C (77.5-80°F) (seatemperatures.net). Beach-weather.com gives 77.7°F. A heated pool is more comfortable for laps.
  • Wind and sea state: the east-southeast trade winds typically blow 12-20 mph. February winds and swells are 'a bit higher' and the sea 'a little choppier' (VisitTCI). Passing winter fronts can shift the wind and roughen the north-shore beaches, including Grace Bay; on those days the south-coast beaches (Sapodilla Bay, Taylor Bay, Long Bay) are usually calm.
  • Sargassum: seasonal, appearing in late spring and peaking in late summer and fall. Grace Bay is 'very rarely affected' even in heavy years, so February risk is low.
  • Sun: UV index 12 is common, meaning sunburn in about 15 minutes unprotected. Shade and umbrella availability matter.
  • Crowds and prices: high season runs December-April, with rates 30-50% above the rest of the year. December-January are the busiest months; February is 'a noticeable change' from those but 'continues to be busy'. Humpback whale sightings peak in February.
  • Calendar: Feb 2-7, 2027 (Tue-Sun) falls before Presidents' Day weekend (Monday Feb 15, 2027) and inside the Tuscany's Jan 5-Feb 9 promo window.
  • Lead time: VisitTCI advises booking accommodation 'well in advance' in high season. With about 3.5 months to go, inventory at top condo resorts may be thin, and the Tuscany's online engine showed no availability ((unverified); call to check).
  • Minimum stays: Tuscany promotions need 5 nights from Jan 5-Feb 9, 2027. Ocean Club has 'minimum stay requirements during holiday and peak seasons'. Windsong's advance-purchase rate needs 4+ nights. A 5-night stay clears the common minimums.

Sources: visittci.comvisittci.comvisittci.comvisittci.comseatemperatures.netbeach-weather.comthetuscanyresort.comoceanclubresorts.comwindsongresort.com

Taxes, fees and getting around

Add 22-27% to any quoted Grace Bay room rate. That is the 12% Hotel & Tourism Tax (unchanged as of October 2026) plus a 10% hotel service charge, and some resorts add a 5% facility fee or a combined 15% service-and-facility charge. Compare alternatives on all-in nightly cost, not headline rate. The airport is about 15-30 minutes away, and a shared airport taxi for two costs about $28-40. A car is optional in central Grace Bay but useful at the east end.

  • Accommodation tax: 12% Hotel & Tourism Tax on all accommodation, confirmed by a law-firm note dated Oct 8, 2026, VisitTCI and current resort rate pages. No rate increase was found in the 2026/27 budget coverage (per search summary).
  • Service charge: the same Oct 2026 note says hotels and hotel restaurants must add a 10% service charge and some properties add a 5% facility fee.
  • Fee examples: Tuscany adds 12% + 10% = 22%. Royal West Indies adds 12% + 10% + 5% facility fee = 27%. Ocean Club adds 12% + 15% combined service charge and facility fee = 27%.
  • Worked example: a $700 headline rate costs about $854 all-in at 22% or about $889 at 27% per night. Over 5 nights that is about $4,270 vs about $4,445.
  • Currency: the US dollar is official, so there are no foreign-exchange fees. Groceries can cost about double typical US prices (VisitTCI).
  • Airport (PLS) to Grace Bay: about 7 miles, typically 15-30 minutes (Tuscany says 15 minutes; VisitTCI says 20-30 minutes depending on traffic).
  • Taxi: government-set shared-van fare from the airport queue is $28 for two people to most Grace Bay resorts (VisitTCI, 2026); extra people pay half fare. Ocean Club's FAQ quotes $36-40 per trip for 1-2 passengers. Expect a 5-15 minute wait while the van fills, plus stops at other resorts.
  • Private transfer: pre-booked SUV service from the airport to Grace Bay starts at $135 (VisitTCI, 2026 price). Taxis are unmetered, so confirm the total for the whole party before departing. A called taxi typically takes 10-30 minutes to arrive.
  • Rental car: not needed for a beach-focused stay in central Grace Bay. VisitTCI says most Grace Bay visitors don't really need a car, and Ocean Club says a car isn't necessary for a short unwind-focused stay. At the east end (Tuscany area) the supermarket is a 5-minute drive and most guests use taxis at night. Tuscany guests get 10% off Grace Bay Car Rentals.
  • Driving notes: TCI drives on the left, but most cars are US left-hand-drive models. VisitTCI says drivers with vision problems should avoid night driving because of glare and reckless high-beam use. VisitTCI puts an economy car at roughly $50/day.

Booking tips

Book direct. Most Grace Bay condo resorts offer best-rate guarantees and direct-only promos, several publish full seasonal rate sheets, and the Tuscany's own up-to-10%-off promo covers exactly Feb 2-7, 2027. Read room labels carefully, because 'ocean view', 'beachfront' and even 'Grace Bay' can mean different things. In condo-hotels, ask for a recently renovated unit, since each one is individually owned. Expect a 3-night or 50% deposit, refundable 21-30 days before arrival in winter. Resorts themselves push travel insurance.

  • Direct-booking perks: the Tuscany offers up to 10% off Jan 5-Feb 9, 2027 with a 5-night minimum. Ocean Club advertises a best-rate guarantee and up to 15% off direct. Windsong offers a best-rate guarantee plus a 10% resort voucher, a 5% member rate, and an extra 7% for advance purchase (60+ days ahead, 4+ nights, non-refundable). Royal West Indies runs early-booking specials.
  • Who publishes rate sheets: Ocean Club (a full grid by view category, including Jan 5-Apr 20, 2027), Royal West Indies (a 'Winter' season of Jan 5-Apr 24, 2027) and The Sands (rates page). The Tuscany shows only 'starting at' prices, so ask for a personalized quote.
  • View labels matter: Ocean Club prices Garden/Pool View, Ocean View and Beachfront as separate tiers, and 'ocean view' is not the same as beachfront. VisitTCI warns that listings advertised as 'beachfront on Grace Bay' may actually be on Leeward Beach or the Bight Beach, both of which are farther from Grace Bay dining.
  • Unit selection in condo-hotels: units are individually owned and decor varies (Oyster on the Tuscany). Ask for a recently renovated unit, and confirm elevator access and floor level if stairs are an issue. Also ask which building is closest to the beach and pool.
  • Pool check for the dad: confirm the pool is heated (February sea is about 78°F), its length and shape for laps, and its opening hours. For example, the Tuscany pool is 70 ft, heated, and open 9 am-5 pm.
  • Deposit and cancellation norms for winter 2027: the Tuscany takes a 50% deposit refundable to 30 days out. Ocean Club gives a full refund to 21 days out for Jan 5-Apr 20, 2027. Royal West Indies and The Sands take a 3-night deposit refundable to 21 days out. Holiday periods are stricter (42-60 days), and advance-purchase rates are non-refundable.
  • Travel insurance: Ocean Club and The Sands both strongly recommend it, because deposits are forfeited inside the penalty window, including for medical issues or flight cancellations.
  • Discounts: no Grace Bay resort we checked advertised a senior discount ((unverified) as a general rule). Windsong's terms list AAA among approved discount rates, so ask. The Tuscany offers special long-term rates for stays of 2+ weeks.
  • Rate comparison: always compare all-in cost per night (rate x 1.22-1.27) and for the full 5 nights, since fee structures differ by resort.

The fine print

How we scored and what to double-check

  • Prices and availability checked Oct 15, 2026. Rates and rooms change often, so confirm the live price for Feb 2–7, 2027 before booking.
  • Sold-out places stay on the page but are left out of the top picks and the best-value line. The table hides them unless you untick “Hide sold-out”.
  • Nightly prices are before tax. The 5-night estimates add each place’s tax, service charge and any resort fee.
  • Who made the list: open for your dates and no more than a 10-minute walk to the sand.
  • Fit score (0–100): each place gets six scores from 1 to 10, judged against what you asked for. The fit score is 10 × their weighted average: beach 22%, beach chairs 18%, pool 18%, cleanliness 14%, newness & condition 12%, service 16%.
  • Best value for the money: no other place on the list is both cheaper and a better fit. Places with no researched price are left out of this.
  • Review snippets are paraphrased, not exact quotes, and dates show when the stay or review happened.
  • “Deep dive pending” places passed a quick screen but haven’t been fully researched; their prices are rough.

What the scores mean

ScoreA 10 looks likeA 4 looks like
BeachBeachfront on a calm, sandy, swimmable stretch4–7 minute walk, or a weaker stretch (seagrass or rocks)
Beach chairsFree, set up by staff, always available in peak seasonFrequent peak-season shortages or towel-saving, or a fee
PoolHeated, 60+ ft, straight and lap-friendly, rarely crowdedSmall, crowded or mostly decorative
CleanlinessReviews consistently say spotlessRecurring complaints
Newness & conditionOpened or fully renovated 2020 or laterVisibly dated in places
ServiceConsistently outstanding, staff praised by nameMixed

Price confidence

  • High confidence: a live quote or an official 2026-27 rate sheet for these dates.
  • Medium confidence: an official seasonal rate from another year, or an aggregator price for Feb 2027.
  • Low confidence: an estimate.
